as_told.title: Bahnson funds T. Townsend Brown's gravity experiments

plain: In the 1950s a North Carolina man named Agnew Bahnson, head of a body called the Institute of Field Physics, paid for the work of an inventor named Thomas Townsend Brown on "gravitators", devices Brown hoped would control gravity. Michels tells this himself across three episodes, without naming a source, adding that the experiments ran at the back of Bahnson's house, that Bahnson wrote of strange phenomena, and that Brown claimed positive results; if so, gravity research was being privately funded alongside mainstream physics.
